# PitCrew troubleshooting

Problems by symptom. Each gives the cause, how to check it, and the fix. For every command, setting
and file, see the [reference](reference.md).

## No warning appears before a compaction

**Cause:** context-watch warns once per level, the first time the context passes 85% and then 95% of
the auto-compaction point. No warning comes when:

- the context has not reached the first level yet;
- context-watch is off, in PitCrew's settings or in the PaceLine file that PitCrew still reads;
- auto-compaction is off, since there is no point to measure against;
- the session started before PitCrew was installed, since the hooks load at session start;
- Claude Code runs under an organization's `sec-default` guard, which skips the hooks module of a
  plugin you install.

**Check:** In the session, run:

```
/pitcrew:context-watch status
```

The first line starts `context-watch on` or `context-watch off` and shows the warning levels. A last
line `settings read from <path> (from PaceLine)` means PitCrew has no file of its own yet, and the
switch and the levels come from PaceLine's.

**Fix:** To turn it on, run `/pitcrew:context-watch config --on`. To warn earlier, add `--levels
70,90`. Start a new session after installing PitCrew. Under a managed Claude Code, see [where an
organization manages Claude
Code](limitations.md#where-an-organization-manages-claude-code-context-watch-does-not-run), and see
[auto-compaction
off](limitations.md#context-watch-leaves-subagent-compactions-alone-and-gives-no-warnings-with-auto-compaction-off)
for the other cases.

## No snapshot after a compaction

**Cause:** context-watch writes a snapshot at each compaction of the main conversation. None is
written when:

- context-watch is off;
- the compaction was a subagent's, which context-watch leaves alone;
- the session started before PitCrew was installed;
- an organization's `sec-default` guard skips the plugin's hooks module;
- the snapshot is there but you look in `.claude/paceline/`, where PaceLine writes its own; PitCrew
  writes to `.claude/pitcrew/`;
- the snapshot is older than the snapshot days, 14 by default, and was removed when a session
  started in the project.

**Check:** Run, with the project's directory in place of `<project>`:

```
/pitcrew:context-watch status --project <project>
```

`snapshots:` names the folder it counted and the number of files. An error inside context-watch,
such as a folder it cannot write, leaves the turn as it was and prints nothing.

**Fix:** Turn context-watch on, check the folder `.claude/pitcrew/` of the project, and raise the
days to keep snapshots longer, for example `/pitcrew:context-watch config --days 30`. See [subagent
compactions](limitations.md#context-watch-leaves-subagent-compactions-alone-and-gives-no-warnings-with-auto-compaction-off)
and [organization-managed Claude
Code](limitations.md#where-an-organization-manages-claude-code-context-watch-does-not-run).

## cache-watch did not start

**Cause:** `/pitcrew:cache-watch on` printed a line that starts `not started`, and exited with 3.
The reason is in the line:

- `no transcript found for session <id>`: PitCrew looks for the session's transcript at
  `<config>/projects/<project>/<session id>.jsonl` and found none;
- `this session has no one-hour cache entry yet`: the main thread has not written a cache entry yet,
  which tells cache-watch the TTL;
- `this session writes five-minute cache entries; cache-watch keeps only one-hour entries`: the main
  thread's TTL is five minutes, whatever its subagents write.

A value out of range stops with `pitcrew cache-watch: lead must be 1-30 minutes` or `pitcrew
cache-watch: max must be 1-20` and exit status 1.

**Check:** Read the reason in the line `on` printed. To see which sessions are watched, run:

```
/pitcrew:cache-watch status
```

**Fix:** For the missing cache entry, take one turn in the session and run `on` again. For the
five-minute TTL, which is Claude Code's setting for the session, run `on` again once the main thread
writes one-hour entries. For a missing transcript, run the command from the session that owns it,
with the same `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` as Claude Code. See [a cache entry
first](limitations.md#cache-watch-needs-a-cache-entry-first), [one-hour entries
only](limitations.md#cache-watch-keeps-only-one-hour-cache-entries) and [the transcript
format](limitations.md#cache-watch-depends-on-claude-codes-private-transcript-format).

## cache-watch turned itself off

**Cause:** `/pitcrew:cache-watch status` shows `off (...)` after the session id. The reason in the
brackets says why:

- `operator`: you replied `stop` or ran `/pitcrew:cache-watch off`;
- `five-minute cache`: the main thread switched to five-minute cache entries, and one wake told you
  so;
- `no reply after N wakes`: N wakes in a row passed without a message from you, which is the limit
  `max` sets;
- `compacted`: the session was compacted, manually or automatically, and the compacted context
  starts a new cache;
- `cache expired before the wake`: the computer slept past the cache's expiry, so the wake never
  ran, and your next message brought a one-line notice.

**Check:** Run the status command. It also lists the other watched sessions, and it removes the
state of sessions whose transcript has not changed for 24 hours.

```
/pitcrew:cache-watch status
```

**Fix:** Run `/pitcrew:cache-watch on` to watch the session again. After `no reply`, raise `--max`,
and read [Choose between cache-watch and idle
compaction](how-to.md#choose-between-cache-watch-and-idle-compaction), since Claude Code can compact
the session about 54 minutes after the last wake. After `cache expired before the wake`, keep the
computer awake while you are away. See [the sleeping
computer](limitations.md#a-computer-that-sleeps-past-the-caches-expiry-loses-the-cache) and [the
self-stop](limitations.md#cache-watch-stops-itself-when-the-main-thread-switches-to-five-minute-entries).

## Every prompt gets two warnings

**Cause:** PaceLine 0.6.0 or an earlier version is installed beside PitCrew, and both run
context-watch: each prompt past a level gets one warning from each plugin, and each compaction
writes two snapshots, in `.claude/pitcrew/` and in `.claude/paceline/`.

**Check:** Run `/plugin` and look for `paceline` among the enabled plugins, then run:

```
/paceline:context-watch status
```

A PaceLine that answers with `context-watch on` runs its own copy.

**Fix:** Update PaceLine to a version that moved the watchers to PitCrew, or turn PaceLine's copy
off after writing PitCrew's settings, as [Run only one copy of the watchers while PaceLine has its
own](how-to.md#run-only-one-copy-of-the-watchers-while-paceline-has-its-own) describes. See
[PaceLine 0.6.0 or earlier runs its own
copy](limitations.md#paceline-060-or-earlier-runs-its-own-copy).
